findings.evidence: UnitInterval.lean:192-196: `set ψ₀ : V → Fin m := fun v => ⟨cellIdx m (x v), cellIdx_lt hm (x v)⟩ with hψ₀` / `rw [Finset.sum_eq_single ψ₀]` / `· rw [indicator_of_mem]` / `intro v _` / `exact rfl`; `Finset.sum_eq_single` leaves main, h₀, h₁ in that order, so the first bullet's `intro v _` addresses the `x ∈ box ψ₀` side goal only. `hψ₀` is never used.
findings.fix: Discharge the membership explicitly, e.g. `rw [indicator_of_mem (fun v _ => Set.mem_preimage.2 rfl)]`, and make the value-level identity explicit with `simp only [hψ₀, Fin.val_mk]` (or a one-line comment stating that `↑(ψ₀ v)` is `cellIdx m (x v)` by `Fin.val_mk`).
findings.issue: In `key`, `rw [indicator_of_mem]` leaves only the membership side goal visible: the main equality `f (fun v => cellIdx m (x v)) = f (fun v => ↑(ψ₀ v))` is closed invisibly by `rw`'s trailing `rfl`, through the `set`-bound `ψ₀` and `Fin.val ⟨cellIdx m (x v), _⟩`. The side goal is then closed by `intro v _; exact rfl`, which unfolds `Set.mem_pi`, `Set.mem_preimage` and `Set.mem_singleton_iff` definitionally. A reader cannot see where either goal went.

findings.evidence: UnitInterval.lean:197-200: `refine indicator_of_notMem (fun hmem => hne ?_) _` / `funext v` / `exact Fin.val_injective (hmem v (mem_univ v)).symm`; `box ψ = univ.pi fun v => cellIdx m ⁻¹' {↑(ψ v)}` (line 180).
findings.fix: Write `exact Fin.val_injective (Set.mem_preimage.1 (hmem v (mem_univ v))).symm` (with the `Fin.val_mk` step for `ψ₀` made explicit as above).
findings.issue: `Fin.val_injective (hmem v (mem_univ v)).symm` applies `.symm` directly to a set-membership proof `x v ∈ cellIdx m ⁻¹' {↑(ψ v)}`, i.e. it uses `Set.mem_preimage`/`mem_singleton_iff` as definitional identities rather than lemmas, and again relies on `↑(ψ₀ v) ≡ cellIdx m (x v)`.

findings.evidence: Basic.lean:118 `exact SimpleGraph.map_adj_apply.2 hij`, :126 `exact fun h => hij (SimpleGraph.map_adj_apply.1 h)`, :184 `imp_congr_right fun _ => SimpleGraph.map_adj_apply`; mathlib/Mathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Maps.lean:96 and mathlib/Mathlib/Data/Fin/Embedding.lean:47-49 (`@[simps -fullyApplied apply] def valEmbedding : Fin n ↪ ℕ := ⟨val, val_injective⟩`), with `Fin.valEmbedding_apply` used in mathlib/Mathlib/GroupTheory/Perm/Cycle/PossibleTypes.lean:46.
findings.fix: Rewrite with the existing `Fin.valEmbedding_apply` (`⇑Fin.valEmbedding = Fin.val`) before applying `map_adj_apply`, or state a local lemma `(G.map Fin.valEmbedding).Adj (i : ℕ) (j : ℕ) ↔ G.Adj i j` once and use it at all three sites.
findings.issue: Three proofs match `SimpleGraph.map_adj_apply : (G.map f).Adj (f a) (f b) ↔ G.Adj a b` against goals containing `Fin.val i` / `(ψ a : ℕ)`, so unification must unfold `⇑Fin.valEmbedding` to `Fin.val`. The defeq is undocumented and is the load-bearing step of the ℕ-detour design; a change to `Fin.valEmbedding`'s definition breaks all three with an unification failure, not a rewrite failure.

summary: Proofs are mostly short and robust (omega/linarith/simp rather than named-lemma chains, no `change`/`show`, no unjustified `revert`), but three spots close goals silently through definitional equality — `Fin.val ⟨_, _⟩`, `Set.mem_pi`/`mem_preimage` membership used as an equation, and `⇑Fin.valEmbedding i ≡ (i : ℕ)` — with no comment or explicit lemma.
